description:
Project Description – Swimming Pool Area Repair & Equipment Replacement
Pasco County, FL
Cause: Flood Damage from Hurricane Helene

This project involves repairs to the swimming pool area due to damage caused by Hurricane Helene. The pool was flooded, resulting in contamination of the water and fiberglass surface with gasoline and other debris. Additionally, the pool pump system was damaged beyond repair and must be replaced. The work will restore the pool to a safe, code-compliant condition without any structural modifications.

Scope of Work with Applicable Codes:
Pool Resurfacing (Fiberglass):

The fiberglass pool surface is stained and chemically compromised from floodwater mixed with gasoline.

Work includes full surface prep, fiberglass coating repair, gelcoat application, and refinishing.
Codes:

FBC Residential R4501.6.6 – Pool surfaces must be cleanable, durable, and chemical-resistant.

FBC Existing Building Code 702.4 – Repairs must not reduce code compliance.

New Pool Pump Installation:

Removal of damaged pump and installation of a new high-efficiency circulation pump.

All electrical and plumbing connections to be updated per code, including bonding and GFCI protection.
Codes:

FBC R4501.19, NEC 680.21 & 680.26 – Circulation system standards and bonding for safety.

FBC Energy Code C403.2.12.1 – Pool pumps must meet energy efficiency requirements.

Deck Surface Cleaning & Minor Repairs:

Removal of flood residue and cosmetic repair of deck coating (no structural deck changes).
Code:

FBC Existing Building Code 702.1 – Work classified as repair, no structural alterations.

Note: This project has not yet started. We are currently awaiting disbursement of insurance funds related to the storm claim. Our attorney is actively assisting with this process. Work will begin once funds are received and permits are approved.

All work will comply with the Florida Building Code (2023, 8th Edition) and Pasco County permitting guidelines.

description:
Scope of Work:
1. Pool Construction:

A 15x30 in-ground concrete swimming pool will be installed with a depth range of 3’6” to 6’.
The pool will feature reinforced walls and floors with #3 rebar for structural integrity.
Includes:
Three (3) water returns
Two (2) main drains
Two (2) color-changing LED lights
One (1) skimmer
One (1) vacuum line
Two (2) back-wall swim-outs
Interior finish: Marquis Pewter Quartz with a lifetime manufacturer’s warranty.
2. Spa Construction:

A 6x6 raised spa will be constructed, featuring:
Six (6) jets
One (1) LED color-changing light
Infinity spillover with a pool trough
3. Pool Deck:

The pool deck will use 24"x24" Nexus White porcelain pavers with matching coping material.
The deck will be installed with a stable 4” base and a ¼” pitch for water drainage.
A 2” Stegmeier Frontier drain with removable covers will tie into the site’s existing drainage system.
4. Screen Enclosure:

A single-story mansard-style bronze aluminum screen enclosure will be installed, anchored to a 12"x12" concrete footer with #5 rebar.
Includes:
Two (2) screen doors with door pads
A 48’ back wall with a panoramic view using durable super screen materials
Connection to the house via a 7” super max gutter
5. Equipment Installation:

Jandy pool equipment, including:
1.85hp Variable Speed Pump
CS200 Cartridge Filter
TruClear 11k Salt Chlorinator
138k BTU Rheem Heat Pump
TCX Automation Bundle for smartphone control
Equipment will be installed on 4” hurricane-rated concrete pads with Schedule 40 plumbing and premium valves for system protection.
Site Modifications:
1. Tree Removal and Replanting:

One existing oak tree will be removed per Pasco County guidelines. A replacement tree will be replanted to comply with local regulations and enhance the property’s aesthetics.
2. Drainage Plan:

The pool deck and screen enclosure gutter system will tie into the existing drainage system to ensure proper water flow toward the right-of-way (ROW). The site’s drainage has been verified as suitable for this project.
3. Landscaping Adjustments:

Existing shrubs along the rear property line will be removed and replaced with a flower bed or plants not exceeding 2’ in height to maintain an unobstructed view of the enclosure.
4. Stucco Work:

The exposed portion of the raised retaining wall will be stuccoed with a scratch coat and brown coat for a clean and uniform finish.
Additional Features:
Floating pool guard alarm.
One-hour pool operation and maintenance training.
Startup chemicals and basic pool cleaning equipment.
All construction and installations will be carried out in compliance with Pasco County regulations and inspected for adherence to engineering specifications.
